vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.claim: Cl-O density at interface is the primary descriptor because it directly measures vacancy-driven halogen redistribution

stoichiometry.Li6 (comp1, comp2): Li6PS5(Cl,Br): 6 Li/fu, 1.0 (Cl+Br), 5 S, 1 P. NO vacancy.
stoichiometry.Li5.4 (comp3-5, modelC): Li5.4PS4.4(Cl,Br)1.6: 5.4 Li/fu, 1.6 (Cl+Br), 4.4 S, 1 P. 0.6 Li vacancy/fu paired with S-site halogen excess.

vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step1_substitution_chemistry: S(2-) + Li(+) -> X(-) (X=Cl,Br): each halogen replacing S removes one Li to balance charge. Hence 0.6 halogen excess <=> 0.6 Li vacancy.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step2_atomic_relaxation_at_surface: When SE slab is cleaved, surface Li and halogen atoms can relax. In Li5.4 family, vacancies within bulk allow surface Li to dive inward (occupy bulk vacancy), pulling Li away from interface plane. Halogens follow the same energy landscape: they prefer to sit at the vacancy-adjacent Li sites (charge balance), which are mostly INSIDE the bulk, not at the surface.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step3_interface_observable: Result: Li5.4 surfaces have FEWER halogens at the contact plane with NCM. Li6 surfaces have NO vacancy to allow this redistribution, so halogens stay at surface. Measured: Cl_surface_fraction comp1=42%, comp2=33%, vs comp3=20%, comp4=25%, comp5=33%.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step4_chemistry_at_NCM: Halogens (Cl-, Br-) at the SE/NCM contact plane interact with NCM oxide oxygen (O2-). Both are anions: REPULSIVE Coulomb. More halogens at interface -> more repulsion -> weaker adhesion -> lower Wad in paper experiments.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step5_quantification: Cl-O bond density (per A^2) at gap_eq, with cutoff 3.5 A. R = -0.914 vs paper exp Wad. Negative correlation = repulsion confirmation.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.step6_collinearity_verdict: Cl-O density is collinear (|R|>0.99) with Li/fu, vacancy count, and Cl+Br stoichiometry. They're all measuring the SAME chemistry: vacancy presence enables halogen retreat from interface.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated.intra_family_limit: comp3, comp4, comp5 all have 0.6 vacancy, same Cl+Br=1.6, only Cl/Br RATIO differs. This is below current resolution (Δ < 0.005 in all descriptors). Paper exp shows comp3 > comp4 > comp5 (Br increase = slight decrease), consistent with Br being heavier/larger and slightly less mobile at vacancy redistribution. But not statistically resolved by our method.

vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.correction_note: Earlier version stated 'Li6 has NO vacancy' which is incorrect: Li6PS5Cl Wyckoff sites (24g, 48h) are ~50% partially occupied even at nominal Li6 stoichiometry. Li6PS5Cl IS superionic (~3 mS/cm at 300 K, Deiseroth 2006), with intracage Ea ~0.12-0.14 eV (Yu/Wagemaker 2016), inter-cage Ea ~0.17-0.20 eV. Li5.4 has ADDITIONAL stoichiometric Li vacancy (0.6/fu) on top of Wyckoff partial occupancy.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.claim: Cl-O density at interface is the primary descriptor. Mechanism = vacancy + halogen size/charge pairing redistributes halogens away from surface in Li5.4 family with mixed Cl+Br composition.

Li5.4_family (comp3-5, modelC).Ea_lower_than_Li6_due_to: additional vacancy + S2->Cl1- weakened Li-anion interaction

vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step1_substitution_chemistry: S(2-) + Li(+) -> Cl(-)/Br(-): each halogen replacing S(4d-position with mixed S/Cl occupancy) removes one Li to balance charge (Adeli 2019). Hence 0.6 halogen excess <=> 0.6 stoichiometric Li vacancy on Wyckoff sites.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step2_correctly_understood_relaxation: Both Li6 and Li5.4 families have facile bulk Li hopping (both superionic). At a CLEAVED SURFACE, however, the question is which atoms TERMINATE at the cleavage plane. In Li5.4 family with mixed Cl+Br, halogen-Li-vacancy pairs (charge-paired locally) preferentially reside in bulk because surface termination forces the pair to be uncompensated. In Li6 family (no extra vacancy) and modelC (Li5.4 but Cl-only, no Cl+Br mix), this pairing argument is weaker.

step3_interface_observable_corrected.key_observation: modelC has Li5.4 family vacancy (0.6/fu) but only Cl (no Br). Its Cl_surface=38% is comparable to Li6 family, NOT to comp3-5 (20-33%). This rules out simple 'vacancy alone causes halogen retreat' interpretation. The driving force requires BOTH (i) stoichiometric Li vacancy AND (ii) Cl+Br size mixture for differentiated bulk vs surface preferences.

vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step4_chemistry_at_NCM: Halogens (Cl-, Br-) at SE/NCM contact plane interact with NCM oxide O2-. Both are anions: repulsive Coulomb dominates at short range. More halogens at the interface -> more repulsion -> weaker net adhesion. This signal is what Cl-O contact density measures.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step5_quantification: Cl-O bond density (per A^2) at gap_eq, with cutoff 3.5 A. R = -0.914 vs paper exp Wad (n=5, p=0.03). Negative correlation = repulsion confirmation.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step6_LBFGS_artifact_corrected: Earlier methods (v9-v22) used unconstrained LBFGS on stacked SE/NCM. Both Li6 and Li5.4 have facile bulk hopping, but at the NCM interface, Li-O coordination in NCM oxide is more favorable than the Li sites in SE Wyckoff partial-occupancy lattice. This sets up a gradient pulling Li from SE into NCM, especially severe for Li6 because (a) frustrated configuration -> larger initial gradient magnitudes (Delta E_config 1162 meV from paper #1), and (b) fully stoichiometric Li means more atoms at the interface to migrate. Constrained relaxation (M2 in v26b) with FixAtoms on NCM + bottom 70% of SE blocks this drift; resulting RMS displacement < 0.2 A all 6 comps, no migration, bond count preserved. This artifact is INTERFACE-SPECIFIC and does NOT reflect bulk Li mobility.
vacancy_mechanism_consolidated_CORRECTED.step7_collinearity_verdict: Cl-O density is collinear (|R|>0.99) with Li/fu, vacancy count, Cl+Br stoichiometry. They all encode the family axis (Li6 vs Li5.4). Within the Li5.4 family (comp3, 4, 5 all have 0.6 stoichiometric vacancy + 1.6 halogen), the residual variation Cl/Br ratio is below current resolution (Delta < 0.005). modelC tells us that within Li5.4 family, the Cl+Br mix matters separately from the bare vacancy.
literature_used: Deiseroth et al. 2006 - original synthesis + structure of Li6PS5X (Angew Chem)
Adeli et al. 2019 - halide substitution boosts diffusivity, Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 conductivity 9.4 mS/cm vs 2.5 for Li6PS5Cl, mechanism = weakened Li-anion + extra Li vacancy + site disorder
Yu/Wagemaker et al. 2016 - Li6PS5Cl bulk vs interface diffusion, intracage Ea 0.12-0.14 eV, intercage 0.17-0.20 eV (PMID 27511442)
Hanghofer et al. 2019 - substitutional disorder + 7Li NMR jump rates Ea 0.17-0.32 eV across temperature regimes for Li6PS5Cl (PCCP)
D'Amore et al. 2022 - argyrodite Li6PS5Cl configuration enumeration, ~10^13 distinct orderings for unit cell, Coulomb-energy selection (RSC Adv)
Kraft et al. 2018 - lattice polarizability + ionic conductivity in argyrodites (JACS)
Pustorino et al. 2025 - systematic Li distribution sampling for LPSCl
